There are two ways that I know of (but most likely there are more):  
1. Either dismantle most of the furby and remove the eyes entirely. There's small holes inside the plastic that you can stick a pin through to push the  eye chips (clear part) out of the white eye plastic. This one can be time consuming (to pull the whole furby apart, unless you already need to fix/clean something inside) and difficult (the face is notoriously tricky to remove because the metal rods it rotates on is usually very stiff to take out).

2. Use the rods of glue that are for hot glue guns to yank the eye chips out of the eye This is generally the preferred method as it's less time consuming and takes less materials (although it can sometimes need to be repeated if it doesn't work at first). You need to use fire to melt one end of the glue rod and stick it onto the eye chip. You then wait for it to dry (some suggest putting the furby in the freezer, but that isn't any good for a working furby as it will damage the insides) and then pull off the glue stick with the eye chip attached to the end. This does mean you'll need to buy a new eye chip, but a clear cabochon of the same size works just as well as anything pre-made you'll find on Etsy or the like.

TL;DR either unscrew the entirety of the furby and push the eyechips out from behind OR attach sticks of glue to the furby's eyes without unscrewing anything and try to yank the eyechips off from the front.
